source_metadata.title: Evaluation Pitfalls and Sparsity Limitations in LLM-based Confidence Estimates for Classification

atoms.canonical_statement: The study evaluated sparsity in LLM confidence estimates for classification, its effect on threshold-based evaluation, and a token-probability-weighted verbalization method intended to reduce sparsity.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: We study sparsity as a distinct and critical challenge... propose verbalization logprobs.

atoms.canonical_statement: The evaluation compared vanilla verbalization, top-2 verbalization, consistency sampling, verbalization sampling, and token logprobs as confidence-estimation approaches for prompted LLM classifiers.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Table 1: Overview of the five confidence estimation methods studied in this work.

atoms.canonical_statement: The experiments used the full SST-2 test split (872 examples), the full SST-5 test split (2,210 examples), 6,000 randomly sampled Yahoo! Answers test examples, and 8,604 sampled Amazon ESCI examples.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: From SST-2 and SST-5 we use their full standard test splits... sample 6,000... sample 8,604 examples.

population.label: Four classification datasets totaling 17,686 evaluated examples

atoms.canonical_statement: Qwen3-32B and Claude 3.7 Sonnet were evaluated, with additional experiments enabling reasoning and an alternative verbalized confidence range of 0–9.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: We observe the same behavior using Claude 3.7 Sonnet, and both models with or without reasoning enabled... alternative confidence range (0–9).

atoms.canonical_statement: Consistency sampling generated four class-label responses at temperature 1.0 and used the modal-label frequency as confidence.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: We sample 4 responses ... at temperature 1.0.

atoms.canonical_statement: Verbalization sampling generated four verbalized-confidence responses at temperature 1.0 and used their mean as the confidence estimate.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Confidence is the mean of the sampled verbalized values. We use the same sampling parameters (4 responses, temperature 1.0).

atoms.canonical_statement: AUARC was evaluated under both linear (trapezoidal) and stepwise interpolation to determine how interpolation interacts with sparse confidence values.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Table 2 shows the impact of using stepwise rather than linear interpolation when calculating AUARC.

atoms.canonical_statement: On SST-2 with Qwen3-32B, vanilla verbalization produced only eight unique confidence values, and more than half of predictions had confidence exactly 95%.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: only eight unique values ... with over half being exactly 95%

population.label: SST-2 test split evaluated with Qwen3-32B

outcome.measurement_method: Count of distinct verbalized confidence scores

atoms.canonical_statement: Across the four datasets, 45% to 93% of verbalization-based confidence estimates were concentrated in the five most frequent confidence values.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: 45–93% of confidences are concentrated in the five most common confidence values

outcome.definition: Percentage of predictions assigned one of the five most frequent confidence values

atoms.canonical_statement: For Qwen3-32B, consistency sampling AUARC decreased from 0.808 with linear interpolation to 0.683 with stepwise interpolation, changing its average rank from first to fifth.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Consistency sampling 0.808 1→5 0.683 100

quantitative_result.original_result_text: Linear AUARC 0.808; stepwise AUARC 0.683; rank 1 to 5.

atoms.canonical_statement: For Qwen3-32B, verbalization-based methods lost 0.7 to 4.5 AUARC points when stepwise rather than linear interpolation was used, whereas token logprobs was unchanged.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: verbalization approaches score 0.7–4.5 AUARC points lower with stepwise interpolation... token logprobs ... remains unchanged.

atoms.canonical_statement: The authors recommend stepwise interpolation rather than linear interpolation for AUARC and similar threshold-based evaluations of sparse confidence scores.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: We therefore advocate for using stepwise interpolation rather than linear interpolation when reporting such metrics.

atoms.canonical_statement: Verbalization logprobs computes an expected confidence from token probabilities over the tens and units digits of a verbalized percentage, treating the two digit positions as independent.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: we compute confidence as the expected value over possible digits at each position... treat them as independent as an approximation

atoms.canonical_statement: Averaged across four datasets with Qwen3-32B, verbalization logprobs achieved AUARC 0.736 versus 0.713 for vanilla verbalization, a 2.3-point improvement.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Verbalization-logprobs 0.670 0.234 0.736 1 1.7× ... Vanilla verb. ... 0.713

outcome.measurement_method: Stepwise area under the accuracy-rejection curve

atoms.canonical_statement: Averaged across four datasets with Qwen3-32B, verbalization logprobs reduced top-5 confidence concentration from 92% with vanilla verbalization to 1%.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Vanilla verb. ... %t5 92 ... Verbalization-logprobs ... %t5 1

atoms.canonical_statement: Verbalization logprobs achieved AUARC 0.736 at 1.7× baseline token cost, while verbalization sampling achieved AUARC 0.734 at 6.8× cost.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Verbalization sampling ... 0.734 ... 6.8× ... Verbalization-logprobs ... 0.736 ... 1.7×

outcome.definition: Total input and output tokens relative to class-label-only prediction

atoms.canonical_statement: Spearman correlation between vanilla verbalization and verbalization logprobs averaged 0.89 across the four datasets.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: We find that ρ averages 0.89 across the four datasets.

atoms.canonical_statement: Verbalization logprobs produced 630 to 2,227 unique confidence values across datasets, compared with 8 to 12 for vanilla verbalization.
On SST-2, achieving at least 98% accuracy required rejecting 39.7% of predictions with vanilla verbalization but only 28.1% with verbalization logprobs, retaining 11.6 percentage points more data.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: one need only reject 28.1% ... salvaging a full 11.6% of the data (39.7% - 28.1%).

population.label: SST-2 test split evaluated with Qwen3-32B

concept.text: Rejection rate required for at least 98% accuracy

quantitative_result.original_result_text: Vanilla verbalization 39.7%; verbalization logprobs 28.1%; difference 11.6 percentage points.

atoms.canonical_statement: With Claude 3.7 Sonnet, consistency sampling AUARC decreased from 0.814 under linear interpolation to 0.703 under stepwise interpolation, with rank changing from first to fourth.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Consistency Sampling 0.814 1→4 0.703 100

atoms.canonical_statement: High sparsity in verbalization-based confidence estimates persisted when reasoning mode was enabled for both Qwen3-32B and Claude 3.7 Sonnet.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Sparsity patterns persist even with reasoning, confirming that the phenomenon is not limited to direct prediction settings.

atoms.canonical_statement: Using an alternative confidence range of 0–9 did not remove sparsity or linear-interpolation inflation and generally increased top-5 value concentration.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: The narrower range 0–9 increases concentration substantially... linear interpolation continues to inflate AUARC scores.

atoms.canonical_statement: Verbalization logprobs assumes that each confidence digit is tokenized as a single token, so adaptation may be required for tokenizers with different segmentation.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: The approach assumes that each digit is consistently tokenized as a single token... may require adaptation for tokenizers that utilize different schemes.

atoms.canonical_statement: The method approximates the two digit positions as independent because standard API logprobs expose probabilities only for the generated token path.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Strictly speaking, this expectation should use conditional probabilities... we treat them as independent as an approximation.

atoms.canonical_statement: Sampling-based comparisons fixed the number of samples at four, although the optimal sample count may vary by model and task.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: we fix the number of samples at four... but the optimal number may vary across models and tasks.

atoms.canonical_statement: The study focused on AUARC; analogous interpolation effects on other threshold-based metrics such as AUPRC were not empirically investigated.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: similar considerations apply to other threshold-based metrics such as AUPRC, which we leave for future investigation.

atoms.canonical_statement: Verbalization logprobs requires token-probability access and does not solve sparsity for APIs that expose only generated text.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: requires access to token probabilities; we do not provide a solution ... where logprobs are unavailable.
